breakfast.name: Byrek (Savory Pastry Pie)
breakfast.description: A traditional baked pastry filled with spinach, cheese, or meat. The phyllo-like pastry is layered with filling and baked until golden.
instructions: Sauté onion and spinach in 2 tbsp oil until wilted
Mix in feta cheese, eggs, salt, pepper, and nutmeg
Brush phyllo sheets with oil as you layer them
Place half the phyllo in baking pan
Bake at 375°F for 35-45 minutes until golden brown
breakfast.notes: Keep phyllo covered with damp cloth while working to prevent drying.
breakfast.fun_fact: Byrek is the most iconic Albanian dish and is eaten for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Every Albanian family has their own byrek recipe passed down through generations.
alternatives: All cheese filling for vegetarian version
Butter instead of oil for richer taste

lunch.name: Frikase (Meat and Liver Stew)
lunch.description: A traditional Albanian stew combining veal or pork with liver, cooked in white wine and broth. Rich and flavorful.
instructions: Heat oil and brown meat on all sides
Add onions and cook until soft
Add bay leaves, rosemary, and thyme
Bring to boil, then reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes
Add potatoes and continue cooking 15 minutes
Add liver slices and cook additional 10 minutes
lunch.notes: Liver cooks quickly, so add it only at the end.
lunch.fun_fact: Frikase is a festive dish served during celebrations and special family gatherings in Albania. It represents the resourcefulness of using all parts of the animal.

dinner.name: Tavë Kosi (Baked Lamb with Yogurt)
dinner.description: Tender lamb baked in a creamy yogurt sauce with rice. A classic Albanian comfort dish.
instructions: Mix yogurt with eggs, salt, pepper, and nutmeg
When lamb is partially cooked, add cooked rice to dish
dinner.notes: Make sure yogurt is at room temperature before adding to hot lamb to avoid curdling.
dinner.fun_fact: Tavë Kosi is often called 'the national dish of Albania.' It represents the perfect combination of lamb, which is the primary meat of Albanian cuisine, and yogurt, which is essential to Albanian food culture.

snacks.name: Burek (Cheese Pastry)
snacks.description: A flaky pastry filled with cheese and baked until golden crispy. Often served as a snack with yogurt.
ingredients: 1 lb cheese (feta or white cheese), crumbled
instructions: Mix cheese with eggs, salt, and pepper
Bake at 375°F for 35-40 minutes until golden
snacks.notes: Burek can be rolled instead of layered for variation.
snacks.fun_fact: Burek is found throughout the Balkans and Middle East, but the Albanian version is known for its delicate, crispy pastry and high cheese content.
alternatives: Butter instead of oil for extra flakiness

desserts.name: Baklava (Honey Nut Pastry)
desserts.description: Layers of phyllo dough filled with walnuts or pistachios, baked, and soaked in honey syrup. Sweet and rich.
instructions: Mix nuts with cinnamon and cloves
Layer phyllo in baking pan, brushing each sheet with butter
Top with remaining phyllo, butter each sheet
Cut into diamond or square shapes
Bake at 350°F for 45 minutes until golden
Meanwhile, heat honey, water, and sugar until syrup forms
Pour hot syrup over hot baklava
desserts.notes: The hot syrup on hot baklava creates the perfect texture.
desserts.fun_fact: Baklava is the ultimate celebration dessert in Albania and throughout the Mediterranean. The recipe dates back centuries to Ottoman times.
alternatives: Different nuts like hazelnuts or almonds
Rose water in honey syrup for Persian flavor
Phyllo made from scratch for authentic touch

nonAlcoholicDrinks.name: Kafe (Turkish Coffee)
nonAlcoholicDrinks.description: Strong, thick coffee served in small cups. An important part of Albanian social culture.
instructions: Stir well and heat over medium flame
When foam rises, remove from heat
nonAlcoholicDrinks.notes: Coffee should be finely ground. Don't let it boil over.
nonAlcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Coffee culture is central to Albanian social life. Coffee 'hour' is a time for socializing and catching up with friends and family.
alternatives: No sugar for less sweet version
Double the coffee for extra strong

alcoholicDrinks.name: Raki (Grape Brandy)
alcoholicDrinks.description: A strong spirit distilled from grapes, plums, or other fruits. An important part of Albanian celebrations.
instructions: Crush fruit and place in container
Collect the heart of the distillation
Serve at room temperature in small glasses
alcoholicDrinks.notes: Proper distillation equipment is needed for safety. Homemade raki can be dangerous.
alcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Raki is offered to guests as a gesture of hospitality in Albania. 'Rakia' is also found throughout the Balkans with regional variations.
alternatives: Plum brandy for different fruit base
